event_title: Appling Solar Farm Begins Commercial Operation
event_description: The 25 MWac Appling Solar Farm began generating power in December 2020. The facility is part of the portfolio powering Meta's Newton Data Center through Walton EMC. Silicon Ranch owns and operates the facility using regenerative land management practices.

event_title: Appling Solar Farm Construction Begins
event_description: Construction began on the 25 MWac Appling Solar Farm with approximately 150 craft workers, many recruited from the local community. The project was completed over 8 months despite COVID-19 pandemic challenges.

event_title: Green Power EMC Bacon County Solar Site Operational
event_description: A small Green Power EMC solar site became operational in Bacon County, generating approximately 2,000 MWh of electricity annually, enough to serve about 140 EMC households.
project_name: Green Power EMC Bacon County Solar

event_title: USDA REAP Grant Awarded for Banks County Poultry Farm Solar
event_description: A poultry farm in Banks County received a USDA REAP grant for solar array installation averaging approximately 183 kW. The grant is part of $3.1 million in federal funding for Georgia farms and small businesses to implement renewable energy technology.

event_title: Qcells Announces $2.5 Billion Solar Manufacturing Expansion in Cartersville
event_description: Governor Brian Kemp announced Qcells will invest $2.5 billion in a new solar panel manufacturing facility at Highland 75 Corporate/Industrial Park in Cartersville. The facility will manufacture 3.3 gigawatts of solar ingots, wafers, cells, and finished panels, creating approximately 2,000 jobs. This is the largest solar manufacturing investment in North America.

event_title: Hanwha Advanced Materials Announces $147 Million Supplier Facility
event_description: Governor Brian Kemp announced Hanwha Advanced Materials Georgia, Inc. (HAGA) will create more than 160 new jobs and invest $147 million in a new manufacturing facility in Cartersville to supply the Qcells facility with encapsulant film. This further strengthens Georgia's solar manufacturing supply chain.

event_title: Green Power EMC Ben Hill County Solar Site Operational
event_description: A Green Power EMC solar site became operational in Ben Hill County, generating approximately 2,200 MWh of electricity annually, enough to serve about 150 EMC households.
project_name: Green Power EMC Ben Hill County Solar

event_title: Robins BESS Approved in Georgia Power IRP Update
event_description: The 128 MW Robins Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) was approved as part of Georgia Power's 2023 Integrated Resource Plan Update. The facility will be co-located with an existing solar facility near Robins Air Force Base.

event_title: Robins BESS Construction Underway with June 2026 Target
event_description: Construction is underway on the 128 MW Robins Battery Energy Storage System near Robins Air Force Base. Burns & McDonnell is the contractor with commercial operation expected in June 2026.

event_title: Brooks County Solar Moratorium Active
event_description: Brooks County enacted a moratorium on new solar farm applications, expected to remain in effect until at least February 2025. The moratorium came in response to community complaints about noise and other impacts from existing NextEra solar facilities.

event_title: Brooks County Town Hall on Solar Farm Concerns
event_description: Brooks County held a town hall meeting where residents voiced concerns about solar farm impacts. Residents reported constant high-pitched electrical noise from transformers and inverters at nearby NextEra facilities totaling over 1,700 acres. Attendees requested extended moratorium and stricter ordinances.

event_title: Noise Citation Filed Against NextEra in Brooks County
event_description: A citation was filed against NextEra Energy for noise violations from their solar facilities in Brooks County. Residents complained of constant whining electrical noise from transformers that collect energy from the solar panels. The case stalled after the county inspector died.

event_title: NextEra Solar Farms Operational in Brooks County
event_description: NextEra Energy's solar facilities totaling over 1,700 acres became operational in Brooks County. The facilities were built on former peanut and cotton farms, converting agricultural land to industrial solar use.

event_title: Green Power EMC Bryan County Solar Site Operational
event_description: A small Green Power EMC solar site became operational in Bryan County, generating approximately 10 MWh of electricity annually.
project_name: Green Power EMC Bryan County Solar

event_title: Six Solar Farm Proposals Reviewed by Bulloch County Commission
event_description: The Bulloch County Commission reviewed six solar farm proposals from Paradigm Solar. The proposals represented multiple potential sites for solar development in the county.

event_title: Tabby Power Creates Georgia Energy Trust Fund
event_description: Tabby Power Solar Company's 26-acre solar farm near Pembroke created the Georgia Energy Trust Fund, donating 1.5% of gross receipts to participating counties. Bulloch County was the first to join this innovative community benefit program.

event_title: Live Oak Solar and Guyton Community Solar Operational
event_description: Multiple small solar facilities became operational in Bulloch County including Live Oak Solar LLC and Guyton Community Solar through Georgia Power's community solar program.

event_title: Amazon Announces First Georgia Solar Project in Burke County
event_description: Amazon announced its first solar project in Georgia, a 70 MW facility in Burke County. The project represents Amazon's commitment to renewable energy and will help power AWS operations.

event_title: Amazon First Georgia Solar Project Becomes Operational
event_description: Amazon's first Georgia solar project, a 70 MW facility in Burke County, became operational. The project supports Amazon's goal of powering operations with 100% renewable energy.

event_title: Second Amazon Solar Project Announced for Burke County
event_description: Amazon announced a second solar project in Burke County in July 2023, building on the success of their first Georgia solar facility.

event_title: Burke County Adopts 90-Day Solar Moratorium
event_description: Burke County adopted a 90-day moratorium on solar development to allow time to review and update the county's zoning ordinance for solar facilities. The moratorium was a temporary measure to develop appropriate regulations.

event_title: Burke County Updates Solar Zoning Ordinance
event_description: After the 90-day moratorium, Burke County adopted updated solar zoning regulations including conditional use requirements requiring Board of Commissioners approval and 10-foot setback requirements while maintaining agricultural zoning.

event_title: Bird Dog Solar and White Oak Solar Operational
event_description: Bird Dog Solar (Heelstone Renewable Energy) and White Oak Solar LLC became operational in Burke County. White Oak Solar's 516-acre facility generated $916,643 in property taxes in 2019 compared to only $8,224 without solar panels.

event_title: Waynesboro Approves Georgia Power Substation Site
event_description: The City of Waynesboro approved a 21-acre site for a Georgia Power substation that could support expansion of the Bird Dog Solar facility to potentially 650+ acres.

event_title: Lancaster Solar Farm Achieves Commercial Operation
event_description: The 80 MWac Lancaster Solar Farm in Calhoun County achieved commercial operation. The project is part of the portfolio providing 100% renewable energy to Meta's Newton Data Center through Walton EMC. Silicon Ranch owns and operates the facility.

event_title: Construction Begins on Lancaster Solar Farm
event_description: McCarthy Building Companies began construction on the 80 MWac Lancaster Solar Farm for Silicon Ranch. The company hired over 500 craft workers for this project and companion Snipesville II, with preference for local and veteran workers.

event_title: Georgia Power Announces Kings Bay Naval Station Solar Project
event_description: The Department of Defense announced the Navy has signed a deal with Georgia Power to develop a 30 MW (AC) solar generation farm at Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay. The $75 million project will be constructed on 258 acres.

event_title: Kings Bay Naval Station Solar Farm Becomes Operational
event_description: Georgia Power's 30 MW solar farm at Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay became operational. The facility routes power to Georgia Power's transmission lines to benefit customers and supports Navy renewable energy goals.

event_title: Green Power EMC Camden County Solar Site Operational
event_description: A small Green Power EMC solar site became operational in Camden County, generating approximately 200 MWh of electricity annually, enough to serve about 14 EMC households.
project_name: Green Power EMC Camden County Solar

event_title: Silicon Ranch Metter Agrivoltaics Project Unanimously Rejected
event_description: The Candler County Board of Commissioners unanimously rejected SR Metter LLC's application to rezone approximately 1,035 acres from AG-3 to Light Industrial for the Metter Agrivoltaics Project. Despite Silicon Ranch offering $100M investment, 200 jobs, agrivoltaics with sheep grazing, and $1M+ surety bond, the request was denied.

event_title: Silicon Ranch Considers Reapplication with $4M Community Benefit Fund
event_description: Silicon Ranch announced it is considering reapplying for the Metter Agrivoltaics Project with a new $4 million Community Benefit Fund. Local community members would have input on how funds are used for job training, health programs, and education.

event_title: Live Oak Solar Operational Near Metter
event_description: Live Oak Solar LLC (NextEra) became operational near Metter in Candler County, providing utility-scale solar generation.

event_title: Savannah Awarded $156M EPA Solar for All Grant
event_description: The City of Savannah, as part of the Georgia BRIGHT Communities Coalition, was awarded a $156 million EPA Solar for All grant in December 2025 to expand solar access for low-income residents and communities.

event_title: Cherry Street Energy SEPA Amendment Approved for County Solar
event_description: Chatham County government approved a Cherry Street Energy SEPA amendment for additional municipal solar facilities, expanding on the successful 2024 pilot program that saved $8,155 in electricity costs across 4 county facilities.

event_title: Georgia Power Community Solar Farm Near Savannah Operational
event_description: Georgia Power's Community Solar program includes a 3.6 MW farm near Savannah as part of 8 MW constructed statewide. The program allows customers to subscribe to solar without installing panels on their property.

event_title: IKEA Savannah Solar Installation Operational
event_description: IKEA's Savannah location operates a solar installation as part of the company's renewable energy commitments.

event_title: Fort Stewart 13 MW BESS Demonstration Project in Development
event_description: Fort Stewart Army Installation has a 13 MW battery energy storage system (BESS) demonstration project in development to improve installation resilience and energy security.

event_title: Seven-Acre Solar Farm Construction Begins in Lyerly
event_description: Construction began on a 7-acre solar farm near Lyerly with approximately 4,400 photovoltaic panels. The project was described as one of the bigger solar farms for North Georgia at the time. The facility was part of Georgia Power's solar program.

event_title: United Renewable Energy Completes 3.8 MW Solar Projects
event_description: United Renewable Energy LLC completed construction on two solar photovoltaic projects in Chattooga County (near Trion) and Stephens County totaling over 3.8 MW on approximately 30 acres. Both projects were financed by United Community Bank.

event_title: Chattooga Solar Plants Sold to Cherry Street Energy
event_description: United Renewable Energy agreed to sell the solar power plant in Lyerly (Chattooga County) and another in Stephens County to Cherry Street Energy. Cherry Street Energy owns, operates, and maintains over 100 solar power systems across the Southeast.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves McGrau Ford Phase I BESS in 2022 IRP
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved the McGrau Ford Phase I Battery Energy Storage System (265 MW) as part of Georgia Power's 2022 Integrated Resource Plan. The project will be located on Georgia Power-owned land in Cherokee County.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves McGrau Ford Phase II BESS in 2023 IRP Update
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved the McGrau Ford Phase II Battery Energy Storage System (265 MW) as part of Georgia Power's 2023 IRP Update. This doubles the capacity at the McGrau Ford site to 530 MW total.

event_title: Georgia Power Breaks Ground on 530 MW McGrau Ford BESS Facility
event_description: Georgia Power hosted company and project leaders, as well as local and state elected officials, for a groundbreaking ceremony at the McGrau Ford Battery Facility in Cherokee County. This 530-megawatt battery energy storage system will consist of two phases with projected commercial operation dates in September-October 2026. Burns & McDonnell is the engineer and constructor.

event_title: Athens-Clarke County Passes 100% Clean Energy by 2035 Resolution
event_description: Athens-Clarke County passed a resolution targeting 100% clean and renewable energy by 2035, establishing one of the most ambitious clean energy goals in Georgia.

event_title: SPLOST 2020 Allocates $16M for Renewable Energy Projects
event_description: Athens-Clarke County's SPLOST 2020 allocated approximately $16 million for renewable energy projects, funding solar installations on government buildings.

event_title: ACC Library Solar Installation Operational
event_description: Athens-Clarke County's library solar installation became operational, saving approximately $25,000 annually and reducing 100 tons of CO2 emissions.

event_title: Costa Building Solar Installation Dedicated
event_description: Athens-Clarke County dedicated solar installations at the Costa Building in May/June 2025, continuing the county's progress toward its 100% clean energy goal.

event_title: ACC Expedited Permit Process for Residential Solar Implemented
event_description: Athens-Clarke County implemented an expedited permit process for residential solar PV systems to reduce barriers to solar adoption.

event_title: Silicon Ranch Clay Solar Project Announced with $89M Investment
event_description: Lt. Governor Casey Cagle announced Silicon Ranch's $89 million investment in Clay County for a 106 MW solar project. The project consists of two sites west of Bluffton producing power for Green Power EMC. The announcement included commitments for REACH Scholarships and community contributions.

event_title: Clay Solar Project Begins Commercial Operation
event_description: The 106 MWac Clay Solar Project began commercial operation in late 2022. The project generates energy for 17,000+ EMC households and pioneered Silicon Ranch's Regenerative Energy approach in partnership with neighboring White Oak Pastures.

event_title: Clay Solar Project Dedication Ceremony
event_description: Green Power EMC, Silicon Ranch, and local officials held a dedication ceremony for the 106 MW Clay Solar Project. State Rep. Gerald Greene, County Commissioners, and Development Authority attended. White Oak Pastures owner Will Harris spoke about regenerative agriculture partnership.

event_title: Silicon Ranch Establishes Gopher Tortoise Sanctuary
event_description: Silicon Ranch developed and funded a private gopher tortoise sanctuary in partnership with Georgia Department of Natural Resources on company-owned lands in Clay County, relocating gopher tortoises from surrounding projects.

event_title: Coffee County Develops Enhanced Solar Ordinance
event_description: Coffee County attorney began developing an enhanced solar ordinance to balance citizen protection with allowing solar development. The effort was motivated by problems in neighboring Jeff Davis County including road damage, farmland conversion, and citizen complaints. The ordinance restricts solar to Agricultural zoning only.

event_title: Georgia Power 200 MW Coffee County Facility Approved
event_description: Georgia Power received PSC approval for a 200 MW solar facility in Coffee County under the CARES 2023 program. The facility will operate under a 30-year power purchase agreement.

event_title: Odom Solar Farm Construction Begins Near Moultrie
event_description: Silicon Ranch and PCL began construction on the 20 MW Odom Solar Farm near Moultrie/Berlin on Bill May Road. The project is part of the portfolio powering Meta's Newton Data Center.

event_title: Odom Solar Farm Achieves Commercial Operation
event_description: The 20 MW Odom Solar Farm achieved commercial operation in December 2021. The Development Authority welcomed the project for tax base expansion and economic development benefits.

event_title: Columbia Substation Solar Farm Operational
event_description: The Columbia Substation solar farm became operational in the Appling area of Columbia County.

event_title: Bijan Solar 39-Acre Proposal Reconsidered with Larger Buffers
event_description: Bijan Solar LLC's proposed 39-acre facility near Patriots Park was reconsidered by the Planning Commission with larger buffers after initial disapproval. Community opposition centered on the populated area location, property values, and wildlife impacts.

event_title: Planning Commission Disapproves Bijan Solar Proposal
event_description: Columbia County Planning Commission initially disapproved the Bijan Solar LLC proposal for a 39-acre solar facility near Patriots Park due to community concerns about the location in a populated area.

event_title: Opdenergy Proposes 476 MW Solar Farm Near Chattahoochee Bend State Park
event_description: Opdenergy, a renewable energy company, proposed a 476 MW, 2,500-acre solar farm near Chattahoochee Bend State Park. The project would be located on land zoned for rural conservation currently owned by Jupiter Timberlands. If approved, this would be the largest solar farm in Georgia. The solar facility would occupy the land for 40 years.

event_title: Coweta County Solar Ordinance Public Hearing Held with Community Opposition
event_description: A public hearing was held at the Coweta County Board of Commissioners' meeting regarding a proposed solar ordinance. Residents spoke in opposition to the ordinance's allowance for rezoning requests. Opdenergy representative Braden Houston advocated for allowing solar development on rural conservation land. The draft ordinance restricts large-scale solar farms on rural conservation zoned land, which developers say functionally prohibits solar development.

event_title: Coweta County Work Session on Solar Ordinance
event_description: The Coweta County Board of Commissioners held a work session to discuss the proposed solar energy system and facilities ordinance. Discussion focused on restrictions for rural conservation zoned land, setback requirements, and acreage caps. Commissioner Al Smith supported a 500-acre maximum for solar facilities.

event_title: Coweta County Extends Solar Ordinance Public Hearing
event_description: The Coweta County Board of Commissioners extended the public hearing on the solar ordinance to their November 5 meeting. Commissioners continue to revise the draft ordinance addressing resident concerns about rural conservation land, decommissioning requirements, and chemical safety.

event_title: Coweta County Schedules Next Solar Ordinance Public Hearing
event_description: Coweta County scheduled the next public hearing on the Solar Energy System and Facilities Ordinance for January 23, 2025 at 6pm. The county has not yet adopted a solar ordinance. Opdenergy has not filed for appropriate zoning for their proposed project.

event_title: Crisp County Power Commission Solar Sites Operational
event_description: The Crisp County Power Commission, serving Cordele and Arabi, has two 1 MW solar sites operational as part of the municipal utility's renewable energy portfolio.

event_title: Crisp County and All Municipalities Adopt Solar Ordinances
event_description: Crisp County and all municipalities (Cordele, Arabi) have solar-permitting ordinances in place allowing solar development in their jurisdictions.

event_title: Decatur Parkway Solar Project Becomes Operational
event_description: Southern Power's 80 MW Decatur Parkway Solar Project near Bainbridge became operational in 2015. The facility uses single-axis tracking technology and is one of two major solar projects in the county.

event_title: Decatur County Solar Project Becomes Operational
event_description: Southern Power's 19 MW Decatur County Solar Project became operational in 2015. Combined with the Decatur Parkway project, the facilities total approximately 950 acres and power about 28,000 homes.

event_title: Decatur County Solar Ordinance with Energy Systems Regulations
event_description: Decatur County has a solar ordinance in place with energy systems regulations. The county serves as a model for other communities, with the Development Authority receiving inquiries from other jurisdictions seeking guidance on solar development.

event_title: DeKalb County Adopts Solar Energy System Ordinance O2018-06
event_description: DeKalb County adopted Ordinance O2018-06, a Solar Energy System Ordinance covering residential and commercial solar installations. The ordinance addresses permitting procedures, setbacks, historic district requirements, and encourages solar orientation in building design.

event_title: Three Dodge County Farmers Receive USDA REAP Grants
event_description: Three row crop farmers in Dodge County received USDA REAP grants totaling approximately $266,000 ($87,000, $94,000, and $85,000) to improve irrigation efficiency by switching to electric engines. USDA estimates combined annual savings of $43,000.

event_title: Two 1 MW Solar Sites Operational in Dooly County
event_description: Dooly County has two solar sites in operation, each producing 1 MW of power. The sites contribute to Georgia's ranking among top states for installed solar capacity.

event_title: Dooly County and All Municipalities Adopt Solar Ordinances
event_description: All of Dooly County and each city (Vienna, Byromville, Unadilla, Pinehurst, Dooling, and Lilly) have ordinances that allow solar in their jurisdictions, creating a comprehensive solar-permissive regulatory environment.

event_title: NextEra Dougherty County Solar Approved After UGA Expert Testimony
event_description: NextEra's 120 MW Dougherty County Solar project was approved in August 2018 after UGA expert testimony addressed community health and safety concerns. The $300 million investment on 1,089 acres is expected to generate $10 million in tax revenue over 30 years.

event_title: NextEra Dougherty County Solar Becomes Operational
event_description: The 120 MW NextEra Dougherty County Solar facility on Moultrie Road/Spring Flat Road became operational in December 2020, fulfilling the $300 million investment commitment.

event_title: Second Solar Farm Proposed in Putney Area
event_description: A second solar farm was proposed in 2023 in the Putney area of Dougherty County under an EDC project. The 16-year lease agreement offers an $11 million tax increase for the county.

event_title: Turnipseed Solar Farm Becomes Operational in Douglas County
event_description: The Turnipseed Solar Farm, a 3.9 MW solar facility developed by Velo Solar and funded by Cox Enterprises as part of their Cox Conserves sustainability program, became operational in Douglasville. The farm generates approximately 5,000 megawatt hours of electricity annually, serving about 350 EMC households. The project represents approximately $7 million of Cox's $25 million partnership investment in solar farms across Georgia and Florida.

event_title: Cox Enterprises Ribbon Cutting for Turnipseed Solar Farm
event_description: Cox Enterprises held a ribbon-cutting event for the Turnipseed Solar Farm in Douglasville as part of its Cox Conserves sustainability program. Neighbors were relieved the property was developed as a solar farm rather than a subdivision. The remaining property was donated into conservation for potential bike trail and park development.

event_title: Governor Kemp Announces $150 Million Silicon Ranch Investment
event_description: Governor Brian Kemp announced Silicon Ranch's commitment to invest approximately $150 million in three solar projects in Early County. The announcement was made as "A New Day in Rural Georgia powered by the sun." The first project, a 102.5 MW solar farm for Walton EMC to support Facebook's data center, was already under construction.

event_title: Bancroft Station Solar Farm Achieves Commercial Operation
event_description: Silicon Ranch's Bancroft Station Solar Farm (102.5 MW) became operational, the first of its projects serving Meta's Newton County data center. The facility is Silicon Ranch's first Regenerative Energy certified project, employing over 675 workers during construction. Modules were sourced from Hanwha Q CELLS in Whitfield County.

event_title: Silicon Ranch and PCL to Construct 20 MW Arlington I Solar Farm
event_description: Silicon Ranch and PCL Construction announced partnership to construct the 20 MW Arlington I Solar Farm for Green Power EMC. The project would provide low-cost solar energy to more than 30 Georgia EMCs across the state.

event_title: Arlington I Solar Farm Achieves Commercial Operation
event_description: The 20 MW Arlington I Solar Farm became operational, serving Green Power EMC and providing solar energy to multiple Georgia EMCs. This was Silicon Ranch's second major project in Early County.

event_title: Effingham County Adopts 3-Month Solar Farm Moratorium
event_description: Effingham County adopted Resolution 022-026 establishing a 3-month moratorium on solar farm applications. The moratorium was implemented to allow time for the county to develop appropriate solar regulations and ordinances.

event_title: Planning Commission Recommends Denial of 150 MW Hester Hill Solar
event_description: The Elbert County Planning and Zoning Commission recommended denial (4-1 vote) of the proposed Hester Hill Solar project by NextEra Energy. The 150 MW project on 2,100 acres with $200M investment faced opposition over environmental concerns, property values, and setting precedent. Residents expressed concerns that Elbert County would become "the mirror capital of the world."

event_title: Sonny Solar LLC Conditional Use Approved Unanimously
event_description: The Elbert County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved a conditional use permit for Sonny Solar LLC. This was a separate, smaller project from the previously contested Hester Hill Solar proposal.

event_title: Fayette County Development Committee Approves One-Year Solar Farm Moratorium
event_description: The Development Committee of the Fayette County Commission approved a motion for a one-year moratorium on solar farms after a resident expressed concerns about an 830-acre solar farm proposal near his property on Payne Road. Chairman Rob Sills stated the county should set a moratorium and then determine how to regulate solar farms. The motion passed and was sent to the full commission.

event_title: Fayette County Full Commission Considers Solar Farm Moratorium
event_description: The Fayette County Board of Commissioners considered the one-year solar farm moratorium that was approved by the Development Committee on February 12. The moratorium was triggered by resident concerns about an 830-acre solar farm proposal and property value impacts.

event_title: Georgia Power Announces Hammond BESS Project at Former Coal Plant
event_description: Georgia Power announced plans for the Hammond Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), a 57.5 MW project at the decommissioned Plant Hammond site in Floyd County. The project leverages existing coal plant infrastructure to reduce deployment time and avoid additional capital investment.

event_title: Georgia PSC Unanimously Approves Hammond BESS Project
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission unanimously approved Georgia Power's Hammond BESS project. Construction is underway with an expected operational date of November 2026. The 57.5 MW battery storage system will provide rapidly dispatchable power.

event_title: Fulton County Signs 20-Year Solar Energy Procurement Agreement with Cherry Street Energy
event_description: Fulton County signed a 20-year Solar Energy Procurement Agreement (SEPA) with Atlanta-based Cherry Street Energy. Under the agreement, Cherry Street will install, own, operate and maintain solar panels on county facilities at no upfront cost to the county, selling electricity at rates lower than commercial utilities.

event_title: Cherry Street Energy Installs Initial 7 Solar Systems on Fulton County Facilities
event_description: Cherry Street Energy completed installation of solar panels on the first seven Fulton County facilities under the SEPA agreement. The initial installations have saved the county more than $130,000 in electricity costs.

event_title: Fulton County Unanimously Approves Battery Storage Resilience Hub at Metropolitan Library
event_description: The Fulton County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved a project to add battery storage to the Metropolitan Library's existing solar array, transforming it into a clean energy resilience hub. The battery system will enhance resilience against grid outages. A $300,000 grant from the Southeast Sustainability Directors Network and Global Philanthropy Partnership supports the installation. Since 2021, the solar array has offset 365 tons of carbon.

event_title: Fulton County Approves Expansion to 46 Additional Solar Installations
event_description: The Fulton County Board of Commissioners approved amending the contract with Cherry Street Energy to add solar panels at 46 additional county-owned facilities. This expansion will bring the total to 53 county facilities with solar panels, expected to save taxpayers $2.4 million over 20 years. The new systems will generate approximately 6.8 million kilowatt hours annually.

event_title: Fulton County Holds Solar Expansion Ribbon-Cutting at Cascade Library
event_description: Fulton County held a ceremonial ribbon-cutting event at the Evelyn G. Lowery Library at Cascade to celebrate the kickoff of 46 new solar panel installations on county facilities. Cherry Street Energy CEO Michael Chanin noted the panels are manufactured by Qcells in Dalton, Georgia.

event_title: Fulton County Celebrates Solar Installation at Dorothy C. Benson Senior Complex
event_description: Fulton County held a second ceremonial event at the Dorothy C. Benson Senior Multipurpose Complex in Sandy Springs to highlight the solar panel expansion. The Benson Complex was the first of the 46 new locations where solar panels were installed and running. The project will create 150 jobs across Fulton County.

event_title: Energiya Global 79+ Acre Solar Farm Approved Near Brunswick Airport
event_description: Energiya Global Capital's proposed 79+ acre solar farm was approved near the Brunswick Golden Isles Airport. The project was expected to create 200-300 construction jobs and 5 permanent STEM positions, supported by the Golden Isles Development Authority as an economic development project.

event_title: USDA REAP Grant Awarded for Southeast Georgia Veterinary Clinic Solar
event_description: Southeast Georgia Veterinary Clinic received USDA REAP funding for a 37.23 kW solar array installation. The grant was part of $3.1 million in federal funding distributed to Georgia farms and small businesses for renewable energy.

event_title: Gordon County Manager Notes Increasing Solar Farm Interest
event_description: Gordon County Manager acknowledged increasing interest in solar farm development and noted that other Georgia jurisdictions have adopted regulations addressing glare, setbacks, and vegetative screens. No formal ordinance or project proposals followed.

event_title: AES Proposes Sweet Magnolia Solar 150 MW Project
event_description: AES proposed the Sweet Magnolia Solar project, a 150 MW facility on approximately 1,260 acres (0.42% of county land). Located about 3 miles south of the Devereux Community, the project would power approximately 30,000 homes annually and provide long-term tax revenue and construction jobs.

event_title: Houston Solar Project 68 MW Becomes Operational Along I-75
event_description: Silicon Ranch's Houston Solar Project (68 MW on 705 acres) became operational along I-75 near Elko. The project features approximately 1,000 Katahdin sheep in an innovative agrivoltaics program, making it Silicon Ranch's flagship regenerative energy demonstration site.

event_title: Houston Solar Project Lambing Barn Completed
event_description: Silicon Ranch completed a lambing barn at the Houston Solar Project, expanding the agrivoltaics program. The facility supports sheep grazing operations and has hosted tours for student groups and the Georgia Young Farmers Association.

event_title: Silicon Ranch Proposes 4,700-Acre SR Robins Solar Farm
event_description: Silicon Ranch announced plans for SR Robins Solar, a 280 MW project on 4,700 acres near Kathleen, which would be one of the largest solar installations in Georgia. The company proposed fencing 2,100 acres for panels while preserving over 2,500 acres unfenced including 700 acres of wetlands.

event_title: Board of Zoning and Appeals Recommends Denial of SR Robins Solar
event_description: The Houston County Board of Zoning and Appeals voted to give an unfavorable recommendation for the SR Robins Solar project. UGA graduate student Ben Carr presented research on the isolated black bear population in the Oaky Woods WMA area, showing bears regularly roam the proposed site. Only one person spoke in support while many opposed.

event_title: Houston County Commissioners Unanimously Reject SR Robins Solar
event_description: The Houston County Board of Commissioners unanimously voted to disapprove the SR Robins Solar project rezoning request. Commissioner Gail Robinson cited concerns about compatibility with the adjacent Oaky Woods WMA and the isolated black bear population. The decision also referenced Silicon Ranch lawsuits in other Georgia counties over erosion issues.

event_title: Green Power EMC Solar Parking Canopy with EV Chargers Operational
event_description: Green Power EMC's solar parking canopy with four electric vehicle chargers became operational in Jackson County. The facility generates approximately 70 MWh annually and serves about 5 EMC households.
project_name: Green Power EMC Jackson Solar Canopy

event_title: Green Power EMC Solar Site with Battery Storage Operational
event_description: Green Power EMC's larger solar facility with 0.25 MW/0.5 MWh battery storage became operational in Jackson County. The facility generates approximately 2,190 MWh annually and serves about 150 EMC households.
project_name: Green Power EMC Jackson Solar with Battery

event_title: Hazlehurst I Solar Farm 52 MW Achieves Commercial Operation
event_description: Silicon Ranch's Hazlehurst I Solar Farm (52 MW, first phase 20 MW) became operational near Hazlehurst for Green Power EMC. The project marked Silicon Ranch's entry into Jeff Davis County as a major solar development hub.

event_title: Hazlehurst II Solar Farm Expands to 72 MW Combined
event_description: Silicon Ranch's Hazlehurst II Solar Farm became operational, bringing the combined Hazlehurst I & II capacity to 72 MW on approximately 750 acres. The facilities feature over 720,000 solar modules and power 8,500+ homes for Green Power EMC.

event_title: Snipesville I Solar Farm 86 MW Achieves Commercial Operation
event_description: Silicon Ranch's Snipesville I Solar Farm (86 MW) became operational, employing over 250 workers during construction. The project is part of the portfolio serving Walton EMC and Meta's Newton County data center through Green Power EMC.

event_title: Snipesville II Solar Farm 107 MW Becomes Largest in Georgia
event_description: Silicon Ranch's Snipesville II Solar Farm (107 MW) became operational, making it the largest solar farm in Georgia at the time. McCarthy Building Companies constructed the facility, hiring over 500 craft workers including local recruits and military veterans. The project serves Meta's Newton County data center.

event_title: NextEra Proposes Brooker Trail Solar 200 MW Project
event_description: NextEra Energy Resources proposed the Brooker Trail Solar project, a 200 MW facility on approximately 1,500 acres. Subject to local and state approvals, the project would create up to 300 construction jobs and provide approximately $30 million in additional revenue for Jeff Davis County. Operations expected December 2026.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves 200 MW Solar PPA for Jefferson County
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved Georgia Power's 200 MW, 20-year power purchase agreement for a solar facility in Jefferson County as part of the CARES 2023 program. Some community concerns were noted near Patriots Park about home values and proximity to populated areas.

event_title: Jones County Planning Commission Holds Public Hearing on Inman Solar
event_description: The Jones County Planning and Zoning Commission held a public hearing on Inman Solar's proposed 75-acre solar farm on Skinner Road. Several neighbors attended to share concerns about fire risks, soil erosion, water contamination, and property values. The company proposed an 88-foot setback from road with shrubbery and fencing.

event_title: Planning Commission Unanimously Rejects Inman Solar Proposal
event_description: The Jones County Planning and Zoning Commission unanimously voted to reject Inman Solar's conditional use application. County Administrator Jason Rizner said the company did not address all resident concerns. If approved, the project would be a joint venture with Georgia Power. The final vote is scheduled for January 21, 2025 before County Commissioners.

event_title: Amazon Web Services Purchases 985-Acre Development Site in Lamar County
event_description: Amazon Web Services purchased a 985-acre development site in Lamar County for $270 million, signaling major data center development interest in the area. This purchase prompted the county to evaluate its commercial and industrial zoning codes.

event_title: Invenergy Announces Lakeland Solar Farms Construction
event_description: Invenergy announced construction of two 1 MW solar facilities in Lakeland as part of Georgia Power's Medium-Scale Advanced Solar Initiative. The project created approximately 50 construction jobs during the 2013-2014 construction period.

event_title: Lakeland Solar Farms Two 1 MW Facilities Become Operational
event_description: Invenergy's two 1 MW solar facilities in Lakeland became operational as part of Georgia Power's Medium-Scale Advanced Solar Initiative. The project provides annual property tax payments to Lanier County.

event_title: Laurens County Adopts Solar Farm Ordinance
event_description: The Laurens County Commission adopted a solar farm ordinance with requirements mirroring Georgia Power standards including fencing, property buffers, bonding requirements, and a 180-day abandonment clause for determining if a facility is no longer in use.

event_title: Duke Energy Project Ponderosa $55M Solar Farm First Reading
event_description: Duke Energy's Project Ponderosa, a $55 million solar farm investment at 330 Holly Grove Church Rd, received its first reading before the Laurens County Commission. The project includes a fee structure of $150K/year (years 1-10), $237K/year (years 11-20), and $325K/year (years 21-30).

event_title: Laurens County Sets Solar Farm Permit Fee at $15 Per Acre
event_description: The Laurens County Commission approved a permit fee structure for solar farms with a minimum of $500 and $15 per acre for larger projects. Commissioner Trae Kemp noted solar farms are "extremely unpopular" in his district and cautioned against setting fees too low.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves 225 MW Solar PPA for Laurens County
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved Georgia Power's 225 MW, 20-year power purchase agreement for a solar facility in Laurens County as part of the CARES 2023 program.

event_title: DeSoto Solar Farm Groundbreaking with 400+ Construction Jobs
event_description: Silicon Ranch held a groundbreaking ceremony for the DeSoto Solar Farm, a 250 MW project across three phases on 2,100 acres representing over $220 million in investment. The project created over 400 construction jobs. Phase I serves Walton EMC/Meta partnership.

event_title: DeSoto Solar Farm Phase I Operational for Walton EMC/Meta
event_description: The first phase of Silicon Ranch's DeSoto Solar Farm became operational, providing power to Walton EMC to serve Meta's data center. The site features regenerative agriculture including sheep grazing and beekeeping partnerships.

event_title: DeSoto Solar Farm Phases II and III Operational for Green Power EMC
event_description: Silicon Ranch's DeSoto Solar Farm Phases II and III became operational for Green Power EMC, generating 147,000 MWh annually. The full 250 MW project is now complete with innovative agrivoltaic practices including Roger Howell beekeeping partnership.

event_title: Silicon Ranch Receives Lee County Chamber Partner in Agriculture Award
event_description: Silicon Ranch received the Lee County Chamber of Commerce 2024 Partner in Agriculture Award for its innovative regenerative agriculture practices at the DeSoto Solar Farm, recognizing the company's contributions to the local agricultural community.

event_title: Fort Stewart Solar Facility Operational
event_description: Georgia Power's Fort Stewart Solar Facility became operational, providing solar power for the military installation. The project demonstrated successful partnership between Georgia Power and military installations.

event_title: Fort Stewart 13 MW BESS Demonstration Project Announced
event_description: Fort Stewart Army Installation announced a 13 MW battery energy storage system (BESS) demonstration project in development. The project represents military investment in grid reliability and renewable energy infrastructure.

event_title: Strata Solar Farms Public Hearing Draws 100+ Attendees
event_description: Strata Solar Farms submitted a conditional use permit request that generated significant public interest with over 100 people attending a public hearing. SailView residents expressed opposition to the proposed development.

event_title: Lowndes IDA Solar Farm Becomes Operational
event_description: The Lowndes County Industrial Development Authority solar farm near Valdosta became operational. The facility generates clean energy for the local area. No significant community opposition was documented during development.

event_title: Valdosta Confirms No Local Solar Ordinances
event_description: City of Valdosta public information officer confirms the city has no local ordinances that directly regulate the use of solar power. This indicates a permissive regulatory environment for solar development.

event_title: USDA REAP Grant Approved for 250 kW Poultry Farm Solar
event_description: HengKim Chhay poultry farm in Macon County received a USDA REAP grant for installation of a 250 kW solar array, the largest of six solar projects funded in the northern Georgia region. The project demonstrates integration of solar with agricultural operations.

event_title: USDA REAP Grants Approved for Madison County Agricultural Solar
event_description: Two USDA REAP grants were approved: 3 Porch Farms received funding for a 13.23 kW solar system with $1,808/year projected savings, and a Danielsville location received funding for a 77 kW solar replacement system with $8,229/year projected savings.

event_title: BOC Chair Addresses Solar Farm Rumors in Harrison Community
event_description: Madison County Board of Commissioners Chair addressed rumors about potential solar farm development in the Harrison community, confirming no formal proposals had been received. Any solar farm would require industrial zoning or conditional use approval. This came after neighboring Elbert County denied a major NextEra solar project in February 2024.

event_title: Green Power EMC Solar Site Operational in McIntosh County
event_description: Green Power EMC's solar site in McIntosh County became operational, generating approximately 130 MWh annually. The small-scale project serves about 9 EMC households and offsets 100 metric tons of greenhouse gas emissions.

event_title: Southern Oak Solar Energy Center Begins Operation
event_description: Invenergy's Southern Oak Solar Energy Center, a 160 MW utility-scale solar project north of Camilla, became operational in early 2021. This was the first major utility-scale solar project in Mitchell County and helped establish the county as a solar hub.

event_title: Mitchell County Approves Solar Moratorium
event_description: The Mitchell County Commission approved a moratorium on licensing new solar projects after community opposition emerged to a proposed project in the southern part of the county. Residents raised concerns about noise, appearance, wildlife impact, and effects on the farming economy.

event_title: Mitchell County Extends Solar Moratorium
event_description: The Mitchell County Commission extended the solar moratorium originally passed in February. The extension allows time for developing new ordinance regulations for open-air businesses in agricultural zones that would apply to solar facilities.

event_title: Hickory Park Solar Farm Operational with Battery Storage
event_description: RWE Renewables' Hickory Park solar farm became operational north of Camilla with 195.5 MW solar capacity plus 40 MW battery energy storage system. This represents one of the larger solar-plus-storage projects in South Georgia.

event_title: Tanglewood Solar Farm Operational for C&I Program
event_description: Origis Energy's Tanglewood Solar farm became operational in Mitchell County with 57.5 MW capacity. The project serves Georgia Power's C&I REDI program customers including Google, Johnson & Johnson, Target, and Walmart.

event_title: Georgia Power Approves 260 MW Old Hickory Solar PPA
event_description: Georgia Power received approval from the Georgia PSC for a 25-year PPA for the 260 MW Old Hickory Solar project developed by Pine Gate Renewables as part of the CARES 2023 program. This is a significant addition to Mitchell County's solar capacity.

event_title: Monroe County Passes Solar-Encouraging Ordinance
event_description: Monroe County passed an ordinance encouraging solar energy development. The ordinance established a permitting framework that attracted solar developer interest in the county.

event_title: Monroe County Commissioners Approve Juliette Solar Farm
event_description: Monroe County Commissioners approved a solar farm project near Juliette. The project was made possible by the county's recently passed solar-encouraging ordinance. Local resident Joshua Nichols expressed support for clean energy in the area.

event_title: Battery Energy Storage System Proposed for Forsyth
event_description: A 4 MW/20 MWh battery energy storage system with room for a 6-bay low-side facility and future substation is proposed on 12 acres in Forsyth. The project received USDA Rural Development categorical exclusion approval.

event_title: Green Power EMC Solar Site Operational in Montgomery County
event_description: Green Power EMC's large solar site in Montgomery County became operational, generating 196,220 MWh annually. This is one of the larger EMC solar installations in Georgia, offsetting 146,030 metric tons of CO2 emissions.

event_title: Chatsworth Water Works Commission Solar Farm Becomes Operational
event_description: The Chatsworth Water Works Commission completed a 1 MW solar photovoltaic farm on 5 acres between the main office and wastewater treatment plant. The project was financed with a $3 million GEFA loan at 1.3% interest plus $300,000 in principal forgiveness. The solar farm serves utility operations during peak hours.

event_title: Facebook (Meta) Announces Newton County Data Center with 100% Renewable Commitment
event_description: Facebook announced plans for a nearly 1 million-square-foot data center complex near Social Circle at Stanton Springs. The company cited Walton EMC's reputation for energy innovation as a reason for the location choice. Facebook committed to powering the facility with 100% renewable energy.

event_title: Walton EMC and Silicon Ranch Partnership Announced for Meta Data Center
event_description: Walton EMC announced a contract with Silicon Ranch, one of the nation's largest independent solar power producers, to develop solar facilities to support Facebook's Newton Data Center with 100% renewable energy. Morgan Stanley is also involved in the landmark energy supply arrangement.

event_title: Oglethorpe County Approves 6-Month Solar Moratorium
event_description: Oglethorpe County approved a 6-month moratorium on solar development to address deficiencies in existing ordinance regulations. Issues with runoff from existing solar installations affecting residents prompted the review.

event_title: Zoning Board Recommends Amended Solar Ordinance
event_description: The Oglethorpe County Zoning Board recommended an amended solar ordinance with enhanced protections including: 50% tree cover protection, specific buffers to inhibit runoff (Sections 712.03-712.04), tree removal specifications, 24-month vegetation regulation, surety bonds, and tax abatement consideration.

event_title: Timberland Solar Project Operational on Goose Pond Road
event_description: The Timberland Solar Project on Goose Pond Road in northeastern Oglethorpe County became operational. This is one of two solar farms in the county.

event_title: GreyStone Power 1 MW Solar Facility Rezoning Approved
event_description: GreyStone Power received rezoning approval for a 1 MW solar facility on 6 acres in Paulding County. This represents one of the early solar installations in the county through the electric membership cooperative.

event_title: Pierce Eunice Solar Farm Generating Power
event_description: The Pierce Eunice solar farm at 6530 Timber Lane near Blackshear is operational, generating 910 MWh between September and December 2024. The project contributes clean energy to the local grid.

event_title: City of Blackshear Implementing Solar on City Buildings
event_description: The City of Blackshear is implementing green initiatives including installation of solar panels on city buildings as part of broader sustainability efforts.

event_title: Third Solar Farm Approved for 10 Acres in Polk County
event_description: A third solar farm was approved in Polk County for 10 acres, following two earlier solar farms approved in Rockmart and Cedartown. This marked continued county support for solar development.

event_title: Cedartown Solar Farm Proposed by Beltline Energy
event_description: Beltline Energy proposed the Cedartown Solar Farm, a 3 MW project on 25 acres. The project is in the development stage.

event_title: SOLARCYCLE Announces Solar Recycling and Glass Factory with Accelerated Timeline
event_description: SOLARCYCLE announced a major solar panel recycling facility and 1.1 million square foot solar glass factory in Polk County, creating 617 jobs at the factory. The company announced an accelerated timeline for development.

event_title: Polk County GA S1 LLC Solar Project Under Construction
event_description: The Polk County GA S1 LLC solar project is under construction, adding to the county's growing solar capacity.

event_title: Green Power EMC Solar Site Operational in Putnam County
event_description: Green Power EMC's solar site in Putnam County became operational, generating 2,000 MWh annually. The project serves approximately 120 EMC households and offsets 1,400 metric tons of CO2 emissions.

event_title: Tilden Area Solar Farm Approved - 150 MW on 1200 Acres
event_description: The Randolph County Board approved a solar farm in the Tilden area with approximately 150 MW capacity on 1,200 acres. The project represents significant investment in the rural Southwest Georgia county.

event_title: Gateway Solar Proposed Near Sparta - 250 MW Plus Battery Storage
event_description: RWE Clean Energy proposed the Gateway Solar project near Sparta with approximately 250 MW capacity plus 95 MW battery storage. If built, it would be the largest solar project in Randolph County.

event_title: Fort Gordon Solar Facility 30 MW Operational
event_description: Georgia Power's Fort Gordon Solar Facility became operational with 30 MW capacity, dedicated to serving military installation needs. The project represents significant Georgia Power investment in the Augusta area.

event_title: Georgia Power Community Solar Facility Operational Near Augusta
event_description: Georgia Power's 2.4 MW Community Solar facility near Augusta became operational as part of an 8 MW statewide community solar program. Customers can subscribe to receive solar power without rooftop installations.

event_title: Richmond County GA S2 LLC Under Construction in Hephzibah
event_description: The Richmond County GA S2 LLC solar project is under construction in Hephzibah, expanding solar capacity in the Augusta metro area.

event_title: Seminole Solar Farm Operational in Donalsonville
event_description: The Seminole solar farm in Donalsonville became operational. The facility generated 287 MWh between September and December 2023, ranking #128 out of 139 solar farms in Georgia.

event_title: Lumpkin Solar Farm 100 MW Operational - Serving Meta Data Center
event_description: Silicon Ranch's Lumpkin Solar Farm became operational with 100 MW capacity. The project serves Meta's Newton County data center via Walton EMC and created 300+ construction jobs with IEA as contractor. The project demonstrates Silicon Ranch's Regenerative Energy approach.

event_title: Americus Solar Approved - 9600 Acres Potentially Largest East of Mississippi
event_description: Invenergy's Americus Solar project received approval from Sumter County for 9,600 acres after extensive public hearings. The project encompasses the Cobb/DeSoto/Leslie communities and could become one of the largest solar arrays east of the Mississippi River with 10,000 acres secured. Community response was divided between supporters citing tax revenue for schools and opponents concerned about landscape alteration.

event_title: RE Sumter LLC 150 MW Project Approved - $200M Investment
event_description: RE Sumter LLC (Recurrent Energy) received approval for approximately 2,900 acres along Bumphead/Lacross Roads with 150 MW capacity and a $200 million investment. The project is expected to generate $10 million in lifetime tax revenue.

event_title: NanoPV Solar Panel Manufacturing Opens - 500 Jobs Created
event_description: NanoPV opened a solar panel manufacturing facility in Americus with 500 initial jobs and a $36 million investment. The company targets 2,000 employees by end of 2026, making Sumter County a solar manufacturing hub in addition to generation.

event_title: SA Solar (Samsung) 200 MW Project Approved - $200M Investment
event_description: SA Solar (Samsung C&T) received approval for 1,400 acres with 200 MW capacity and $200 million investment located 7 miles south of Americus. Construction to begin 2025 with operations expected 2026/2027. Combined with Invenergy investment, over $700 million in solar investment in Sumter County.

event_title: Multiple USDA REAP Grants Approved for Tattnall County Agricultural Solar
event_description: Multiple USDA REAP grants approved for Tattnall County: Abundant Grace Farm LLC (45 kW) and Boyette Farms Inc. (21 kW) in Reidsville, and Benjamin Hilliard poultry farm (78 kW) in Glennville. Combined projects replace over 200,000 kWh/year.

event_title: Reidsville Implementing Green Initiatives Including Solar
event_description: The City of Reidsville is implementing green initiatives including solar panels on city buildings and partnership with local biomass plant. The city was recognized as a 'Green Community' by the Georgia Municipal Association.

event_title: McRae Solar Farm 3.137 MW Operational on Converted Timberland
event_description: Beltline Energy's McRae Solar Farm became operational in Telfair County with 3.137 MW capacity on 25 acres of converted timberland. Using single-axis trackers, the project generates 5,332 MWh annually, serving 784 equivalent households and providing 20+ years of lease revenue to landowner.

event_title: Telfair Thompson Solar Farm Operational
event_description: The Telfair Thompson solar farm became operational in McRae-Helena. The project generated 901 MWh between September and December 2023, contributing to the local clean energy portfolio.

event_title: Terrell Solar Farm 74 MW Commissioned by Silicon Ranch and Green Power EMC
event_description: Silicon Ranch's Terrell Solar Farm was commissioned in partnership with Green Power EMC with 74 MW capacity. The project serves 12,000 EMC households and generates 182,000 MWh annually. This represents significant clean energy investment in Southwest Georgia.

event_title: Terrell Riles Stovall Solar Farm Operational
event_description: The Terrell Riles Stovall solar farm became operational in Terrell County, adding to the county's growing solar portfolio.

event_title: Thomas County Adopts Solar Ordinance After Moratorium
event_description: Thomas County adopted a solar ordinance after a moratorium period. The ordinance requires facilities over 200 acres to locate in commercial/industrial zones only. Facilities 200 acres or less may receive conditional use approval in agricultural districts. Requirements include 100-foot setbacks from property lines and decommissioning bonds.

event_title: Thomas County Imposes Indefinite Solar Moratorium
event_description: Thomas County imposed an indefinite moratorium on new solar projects after the first facility approved under the 2017 ordinance was deemed 'a disappointing example.' Concerns included inadequate buffers, inability to police annual bond renewals, and decommissioning responsibilities. The county had approximately 6 solar operations at the time. Commissioner Michael Stephenson noted setbacks 'looked closer than we had anticipated.'

event_title: Thomas County Residents Raise Decommissioning and Bond Concerns
event_description: Community members and county officials raised concerns about solar facility management including: Who is responsible for repair and eventual disposal of panels? How to police annual bond renewals over 35-year project life? County Administrator Chester Hickey noted they were unaware multi-year bonds were unavailable.

event_title: Tift County Declines to Enact Solar Moratorium Unlike Neighboring Grady County
event_description: While Grady County enacted a 60-day solar panel moratorium in February 2017 (later extended in May), neither the City of Tifton nor Tift County established similar restrictions. This permissive stance contrasts with neighboring counties that took action to regulate solar development.

event_title: Green Power EMC Solar Site Begins Operation in Toombs County
event_description: Green Power EMC operates a solar site in Toombs County expected to generate 40 megawatt hours of electricity annually, offsetting 30 metric tons of greenhouse gas emissions and serving approximately 3 EMC households. This is one of multiple Green Power EMC sites in the county.
project_name: Green Power EMC Toombs Small Site

event_title: Large Green Power EMC Solar Facility Operational in Toombs County
event_description: A major Green Power EMC solar site in Toombs County expected to generate 613,200 megawatt hours of electricity annually, offsetting approximately 456,000 metric tons of greenhouse gas emissions. This represents one of the largest EMC solar installations in the state.
project_name: Green Power EMC Toombs Major Site

event_title: Local Veteran Leads Massive 2500-Acre Toombs County Solar Project
event_description: Vidalia native Phillip A. Ceasar, a U.S. Air Force veteran, is leading the creation of a 2,500-acre Solar Panel Farm along GA Hwy 297 in Toombs County. Ceasar works with Terracon consulting and is responsible for overseeing construction testing. Workers are clearing timber and preparing for panel installation.

event_title: SR Toombs LLC Solar Farm Begins Commercial Operation
event_description: SR Toombs LLC solar farm in Vidalia began commercial operation, generating 54.6 GWh during a recent 3-month period. The facility is ranked #44 out of 144 solar farms in Georgia for total annual net electricity generation.

event_title: Towns County Receives USDA REAP Grant for Solar Array Installation
event_description: Towns County was among six northern Georgia locations receiving USDA REAP grants for solar array installations. The grants went to poultry farms and small businesses, averaging 183 kW installations. This federal investment supports renewable energy adoption in rural Georgia.

event_title: Georgia's First Solar-Powered EV Charging Station Opens at West Point
event_description: The PV4EV solar-powered electric vehicle charging station opened at the West Point Visitor Information Center on I-85. This Level 3 quick-charge station can provide 80% battery charge in less than 45 minutes and was developed through a partnership between The Ray, Kia Motors, Hannah Solar, and Georgia DOT. It marked the first of many infrastructure upgrades planned for The Ray corridor.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves 1 MW Right-of-Way Solar Pilot Along The Ray
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved the installation of one megawatt of solar generation in the right-of-way along Interstate 85 in Troup County. The motion was proposed by Commissioner Tim Echols and passed at two sessions with votes of 4-1 and 3-2. Georgia Power will own and operate the project, with construction required by December 2019.

event_title: Nation's First Pollinator-Friendly Right-of-Way Solar Announced for Troup County
event_description: The Ray announced that Georgia Power would construct a one-megawatt solar array at Exit 14 on I-85, becoming the first in the nation to use native pollinator-friendly flowering plants as ground cover. The project would create habitat for honey bees, monarch butterflies and other pollinators for at least 35 years. Troup County partnered to provide vegetative waste material from the landfill as soil amendment.

event_title: Troup County Partners on Vegetative Waste Re-use for Solar Project
event_description: Troup County partnered with The Ray, Georgia Power, and Georgia DOT to contribute decomposed vegetative waste from the Troup County Landfill to serve as soil for pollinator plants at the solar project site. The partnership addresses both landfill capacity issues and environmental goals for the solar installation.

event_title: First Solar Road in the United States Unveiled in Troup County
event_description: The Ray, Georgia DOT, and Colas unveiled an upgraded version of the Wattway solar road at the Visitor Information Center at Exit 1 on I-85. This became the first solar road in America, allowing the road surface to generate clean renewable energy while providing safe vehicular traffic. The technology was invented in partnership with the French National Solar Energy Institute.

event_title: Ashburn Solar LLC Receives USDA REAP Grant for 340 kW Solar System
event_description: Ashburn Solar LLC received a $68,961 USDA REAP grant for a 340 kW solar generation system. The USDA estimates the system will generate 599,662 kWh annually, equivalent to powering 55 homes. This small business project represents the only documented solar activity in Turner County.

event_title: First Solar Announces Largest Solar Project in Southeast US for Twiggs County
event_description: First Solar announced plans for the GA Solar 4 project, a 200 MW photovoltaic solar facility in Twiggs County near Warner Robins. The project would span 2,000 acres and be the largest solar power plant in the southeastern United States. The announcement highlighted Twiggs County's leadership in attracting renewable energy development.

event_title: Origis Energy Acquires GA Solar 4 Project from First Solar
event_description: Origis Energy announced the acquisition of the GA Solar 4 Project from First Solar. Origis will sell all energy and renewable attributes to Georgia Power through the Renewable Energy Development Initiative (REDI) program. The deal positioned Origis as the owner and operator while First Solar continued construction using over 500,000 thin-film solar modules.

event_title: GA Solar 4 Groundbreaking Ceremony Celebrates $210 Million Investment
event_description: Leaders from Georgia Power, Georgia PSC, Twiggs County Commission, Origis Energy, and First Solar gathered for the ceremonial groundbreaking of the GA Solar 4 project. The $210 million investment was celebrated as the largest infrastructure project in Twiggs County history, creating up to 400 construction jobs. PSC Commissioner Tim Echols praised the county's progressive approach to the new economy.

event_title: Local Landowner Celebrates Solar Farm Partnership
event_description: Wayne Christian, a local landowner who sold timber land to First Solar for the project, spoke positively about the development. His family had prior experience with solar farms and praised the community's cooperation. This reflected broad local support for the project among affected landowners.

event_title: Twiggs Solar Becomes Operational as Georgia's Largest Solar Facility
event_description: The Twiggs Solar facility (GA Solar 4) achieved commercial operation, becoming the largest solar power plant in Georgia and one of the largest in the southeastern United States. The 200 MW facility spans 2,000 acres and features over 400,000 First Solar thin-film modules on single-axis tracker mounts. Origis Energy Services operates the plant.

event_title: Origis Energy Donates $25,000 Educational Grant to Local STEM Program
event_description: Origis Energy announced a $25,000 educational grant to A.S.P.I.R.E., a non-profit youth development and mentoring organization in Twiggs County. The donation was part of Origis Energy's philanthropic initiative to support communities hosting their solar installations. A.S.P.I.R.E. focuses on STEM competencies for local youth.

event_title: Sheep and Goats Begin Grazing Twiggs County Solar Farm
event_description: Onward Energy began using Goat Farm Road company to deploy sheep and goats for vegetation management under the solar panels at the Twiggs County solar farm. The agrivoltaics approach reduces costs compared to mowing, decreases emissions, and supports local wildlife including bobwhite quails, rabbits, and foxes.

event_title: First Solar Lawsuit Over $13 Million Rain Damage Claim Goes to Trial
event_description: A lawsuit between First Solar Electric and insurance company Zurich American went to trial in Macon federal court. First Solar sought $13 million for damage caused by five instances of torrential rain between 2019 and 2020 during construction of the Twiggs County solar farm. The case centered on whether rain damage should be covered under flooding or water damage policy provisions.

event_title: Residents Raise Land Use Concerns About Solar Farm Impacts
event_description: Local resident Sharon Lemay expressed concerns about flooding problems that emerged after the solar farm was built across from her home. She stated that tree removal changed the land demographics and caused flooding on residential properties. Similar concerns were raised during discussions about a proposed data center, with residents noting the solar farm's environmental impacts as precedent.

event_title: Georgia Power First Large-Scale Solar Investment Comes Online in Upson County
event_description: A new solar array in Upson County began producing energy for the Georgia Power grid, making it the company's first large-scale solar investment. Rocky Creek Solar is a 1 MWac project developed by Origis Energy for Georgia Power under the Advanced Solar Initiative.

event_title: Upson County GA S1 LLC Solar Facility Under Construction
event_description: Upson County GA S1 LLC solar photovoltaic farm is under construction in Thomaston. The facility will add to the county's existing solar infrastructure alongside Rocky Creek Solar Farm and Camp Solar Plant.

event_title: Walker County Enacts Moratorium on New Solar Farms
event_description: Walker County Board of Commissioners passed Resolution R-018-24 enacting a temporary emergency moratorium on the acceptance of applications regarding solar energy systems. This action was taken to allow time for developing comprehensive solar regulations.

event_title: Walker County Repeals Solar Moratorium After Developing Ordinance
event_description: Walker County Board of Commissioners passed Resolution R-034-24 to repeal the temporary emergency moratorium on the acceptance of applications regarding solar energy systems. The repeal followed development of new land use code amendments addressing solar development.

event_title: Walker County Adopts Restrictive Solar Energy Systems Ordinance
event_description: Walker County Board of Commissioners adopted Ordinance O-01-24 amending the Land Use Code to add a new special use permit requirement for Solar Energy Systems (SES). The ordinance restricts SES to commercial and industrial zoning and requires decommissioning no later than 12 months after a SES has stopped generating electricity.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves Large Scale Solar Program
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved Georgia Power's plan to purchase energy from up to 50 megawatts of solar capacity under the Large Scale Solar (LSS) program. Simon Solar Farm, LLC was contracted to build a 30 MW project near Social Circle.

event_title: Silicon Ranch Social Circle Solar Farm Becomes Operational
event_description: Silicon Ranch's 30 MW Social Circle Solar Farm became commercially operational, more than a year ahead of the 2015 deadline. The ground-mounted solar installation covers approximately 160 acres of a 230-acre site. At the time, this was the largest solar plant east of the Mississippi River. Silicon Ranch worked with Georgia Power to draft the first large-scale solar PPA in Georgia, which became a template for subsequent projects.

event_title: Simon Solar Farm Ribbon Cutting Ceremony
event_description: State and local officials joined Silicon Ranch for a ribbon-cutting ceremony at the Social Circle Solar Farm. Developer Steve Ivey noted he was 'farming again on the land' his grandfather used for cotton, now with clean energy as the crop.

event_title: Bancroft Station Solar Farm Ceremony - First Facebook Solar Project in Georgia
event_description: Facebook representatives joined Walton EMC and Silicon Ranch to 'flip the switch' on the 102.5 MW Bancroft Station Solar Farm in Early County. This is the first solar project supporting Facebook's Newton Data Center operations. Governor Kemp praised the cooperation between Walton EMC and leading companies.

event_title: Silicon Ranch and Walton EMC Complete Three New Solar Farms for Meta
event_description: Walton EMC and Silicon Ranch announced three new utility-scale solar facilities (287 MW total) are now generating renewable energy for Meta's Georgia operations. The Lumpkin Solar Farm (100 MW), Lancaster Solar Farm (80 MW), and Snipesville II Solar Farm (107 MW) are located across southwest and southeast Georgia. This brings the partnership total to 435 MW across six projects.

event_title: Meta Partners with Walton EMC and Silicon Ranch for Three New 560 MW Solar Projects
event_description: Walton EMC announced contracts with Silicon Ranch on behalf of Meta for three new solar facilities totaling 560 megawatts. Silicon Ranch will invest $1.7 billion in Georgia through this partnership. The projects will use regenerative agriculture practices including sheep grazing.

event_title: Chase Farms Solar Project Approved Through Advanced Solar Initiative
event_description: Hannah Solar developed a solar project at Chase Farms in Waycross through Georgia Power's Advanced Solar Initiative (ASI). The project converted fallow farmland that could not be easily irrigated into a revenue-generating solar installation. The ASI program was created by the Georgia Public Service Commission to encourage solar development in Georgia.

event_title: Duke Energy Acquires Ware County Solar Farm from SolAmerica
event_description: Duke Energy Renewables announced the acquisition of six Georgia solar projects from SolAmerica Energy, including the Ware County Solar Farm in Waycross. The acquisition expanded Duke Energy's solar portfolio in Georgia and demonstrated continued investor interest in the state's solar market.

event_title: Ware Avra I and II Solar Farms Become Operational
event_description: The Ware Avra I and Ware Avra II solar farms located at 1469 Pafford Lake Road in Waycross achieved operational status. Ware Avra I is ranked #63 out of 139 solar farms in Georgia by annual generation, producing approximately 1.3 GWh quarterly. The facilities contribute to Ware County's renewable energy portfolio.

event_title: Waycross-Ware County Planning Commission Reviews Comprehensive Solar Ordinance
event_description: The Waycross-Ware County Planning Commission agenda included review of a comprehensive solar farm development ordinance. County attorneys had finalized the draft code addressing solar energy development regulations. The ordinance would establish standards for solar development in unincorporated Ware County.

event_title: PowerUp Program Trains Local Workers as Solar Technicians in Warren County
event_description: The PowerUp Program, led by Blue Ridge Power (a strategic construction partner of Pine Gate Renewables), trained local Georgia residents including Jhalexis Lee and Cameron Swinson as solar technicians. Lee joined after her son was born seeking a better career path as a former warehouse operator.

event_title: Bulldog Solar Farm Begins Commercial Operation in Warren County
event_description: Bulldog Solar, developed and owned by Pine Gate Renewables with Amazon as the energy purchaser, began commercial operation in Warren County. The project employed local workers who participated in the PowerUp Program workforce training initiative for solar technicians.

event_title: Amazon Announces Warren County Solar as Part of Georgia Renewable Portfolio
event_description: Amazon announced that Bulldog Solar in Warren County is now online as part of the company's growing renewable energy portfolio in Georgia. Amazon reported supporting a total of eight projects in the state and announced three additional new projects in Wheeler, Burke, and Oglethorpe counties.

event_title: Azalea Solar Power Facility Acquired and Begins Operation
event_description: Dominion Renewable Energy acquired Azalea Solar Power Facility from Smart Energy Capital and Jacoby Development. The facility outside Davisboro produces 7.7 megawatts fed into a transformer station for Cobb Electric Membership Corp under a long-term power purchase agreement.

event_title: Washington County Solar Site Operational Through Green Power EMC
event_description: Green Power EMC solar site in Washington County expected to generate 14,000 megawatt hours of electricity annually, offsetting 11,000 metric tons of greenhouse gas emissions and producing enough electricity to serve about 900 EMC households.

event_title: NextEra Proposes 200 MW Walnut Branch Solar Project in Washington County
event_description: NextEra Energy Resources proposes the Walnut Branch Solar project for Washington County with capacity of up to 200 megawatts. The project represents significant capital investment and will create jobs and revenue for landowners and the local community once operational.

event_title: Westberry Jesup Solar Farm Becomes Operational
event_description: The Westberry Jesup solar farm in Wayne County achieved operational status, joining Georgia's growing portfolio of utility-scale solar facilities. The facility is located in Jesup and contributes to the state's renewable energy generation.

event_title: Johnson Solar Farm Begins Operation in Wayne County
event_description: The Johnson Solar Farm, a 1.54 MW facility developed by Beltline Energy, began commercial operation in Wayne County. The single-axis tracking system generates approximately 2,695 MWh annually, enough to power approximately 385 households.

event_title: Federal REAP Grant Supports Solar Installation at Crossroads Broilers
event_description: USDA Rural Development awarded a grant for the purchase and installation of a 45 kW solar energy replacement system at Crossroads Broilers Inc. in Jesup. The project will replace 71,080 kWh per year and save approximately $7,463 annually. The grant was part of the Rural Energy for America Program supporting agricultural renewable energy.

event_title: BrightNight Proposes 400 MW Pepper Hammock Solar Project
event_description: BrightNight announced the Pepper Hammock project, a 400 MW solar and battery storage facility spanning 3,100 acres across Brantley and Wayne Counties. The project would generate over $47 million in property tax revenue over 20 years. Public hearings were held in Brantley County, with the company touting job creation during construction and long-term operations.

event_title: Brantley County Holds Public Hearings on Pepper Hammock Solar Project
event_description: The Brantley County Commission held two public hearings regarding the Pepper Hammock solar project, which would span into Wayne County. Citizens questioned BrightNight officials about hazardous materials, disposal plans, and decommissioning. The company indicated Wayne County had already made commitments to the project. The project promises $835,000 per year in Brantley County taxes alone.

event_title: Amazon Announces New Solar Farm in Wheeler County
event_description: Amazon announced a new solar farm in Wheeler County as part of a three-project announcement that also included Burke and Oglethorpe counties. This brings Amazon's renewable energy portfolio in Georgia to a total of eight projects, expanding corporate renewable investment in rural Georgia.

event_title: Yonah Mountain Vineyards Solar Array Operational
event_description: Yonah Mountain Vineyards operates a 106 kW solar array at their tourist destination and wedding venue near Cleveland. The commercial installation demonstrates solar adoption at tourism businesses in the mountain county.

event_title: Qcells Opens Largest Solar Manufacturing Facility in Western Hemisphere
event_description: Qcells opened a 1.7-gigawatt solar panel manufacturing facility in Dalton, making it the largest solar panel manufacturing facility in the Western Hemisphere. The facility produces 12,000 panels a day and supports over 750 jobs in Whitfield County.

event_title: Governor Kemp Announces Qcells $171M Expansion Creating 470 Jobs
