event_description: Governor Brian Kemp announced Qcells will invest $171 million in a new solar module manufacturing facility in Dalton, creating 470 new jobs. The new facility at 310 Nexus Drive will add 1.4 gigawatts of manufacturing capacity, bringing total U.S. capacity to 3.1 gigawatts.

event_title: Qcells Announces $2.5 Billion Investment Including Third Dalton Facility
event_description: Qcells announced a $2.5 billion investment including a third facility in Dalton creating 510 new jobs and adding 2 gigawatts of production capability. Combined with a new Cartersville facility, total capacity will reach 8.4 gigawatts by 2024 with 4,000 employees. This represents the largest single investment in solar manufacturing in U.S. history.

event_title: Qcells Completes Dalton Factory Expansion to 5.1 GW Capacity
event_description: Qcells completed its Dalton factory expansion, adding 2 gigawatts of solar capacity to bring total output to 5.1 GW. The expansion created 510 additional jobs and is the first solar panel plant expansion since the IRA. The factory now produces nearly 30,000 solar panels per day and will manufacture two new products: Q.TRON G2 residential panels and bifacial utility panels.

event_title: Duke Energy Renewables Acquires Abbeville Solar Farm
event_description: Duke Energy Renewables acquired a 1 MW DC / 769 kW AC solar farm in Abbeville as part of a six-project portfolio from SolAmerica Energy under Georgia Power's Advanced Solar Initiative. The facility operates under a 30-year PPA with Georgia Power.

event_title: Dublin Solar I Begins Commercial Operation in Wilkinson County
event_description: Dublin Solar I, owned by Dublin Solar I LLC, became operational in Wilkinson County, contributing to the county's growing solar portfolio alongside other facilities.

event_title: Richland Solar Center Operational in Wilkinson County
event_description: Richland Solar Center, owned by Dominion Renewable Energy, began commercial operation in Wilkinson County, adding to the county's utility-scale solar capacity.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves 183 MW Solar Plus Storage Project in Wilkinson County
event_description: Georgia Public Service Commission approved Georgia Power's request to certify a 20-year PPA for a 183 MW solar facility paired with 91.5 MW battery storage system in Wilkinson County. The project was selected through the CARES 2023 RFP and will be built by third-party developers with expected commercial operation by 2028.

event_title: Coweta County Approves Restrictive Solar Ordinance
event_description: After months of public hearings and debates, Coweta County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved a new solar ordinance limiting solar farms to industrial zoning with a 500-acre cap. The ordinance was developed in response to Opdenergy's proposed 476 MW solar farm near Chattahoochee Bend State Park. A representative from Opdenergy stated the ordinance would effectively eliminate potential for large-scale solar farms in the county.

event_title: Floyd County Commission Rejects Isbell Road Solar Farm
event_description: The Floyd County Commission voted 3-0 to reject a special-use permit for a solar farm on 40 acres of undeveloped land off Isbell Road near Silver Creek. Planning staff recommended denial, noting the land could be better suited for residential development due to proximity to nearby neighborhoods. The rejection was issued 'without prejudice,' allowing the property owner to resubmit a modified request.

event_title: PSC Staff Reports Question Georgia Power Capacity Projections
event_description: Two separate PSC staff reports filed November 12 warned that Georgia Power may be overestimating capacity needs for data centers. The reports stated that if the market shifts or forecasted large loads do not materialize, residential customers would bear the costs. The reports were prepared as testimony ahead of the December 19 PSC decision on Georgia Power's 9,885 MW capacity request.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves Historic 9885 MW Capacity Expansion
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission voted unanimously 5-0 to approve Georgia Power's request for approximately 9,885 MW of new generation capacity. The approved portfolio includes more than 3,600 MW of combined cycle natural gas, more than 3,000 MW of battery energy storage systems (BESS), 350 MW of BESS plus solar, and more than 2,800 MW of power purchase agreements. The decision came after extensive public hearings with emotional opposition.

event_title: Georgia Power Laurens County Solar Plus Storage Project Approved by PSC
event_description: As part of the December 19 PSC approval, Georgia Power received certification for a 200 MW solar facility paired with a 200 MW battery energy storage system (BESS) in Laurens County. This company-owned project is separate from the previously approved 225 MW CARES solar PPA.

event_title: Georgia Power Plant Mitchell Solar Plus Storage Project Approved by PSC
event_description: As part of the December 19 PSC approval, Georgia Power received certification for a 150 MW solar facility paired with a 150 MW battery energy storage system (BESS) at the site of the former Plant Mitchell coal facility in Dougherty County. This repurposes a retired coal plant site for renewable energy.

event_title: Oglethorpe County Adopts Revised Solar Farm Ordinance
event_description: Oglethorpe County Board of Commissioners approved a new solar farm amendment after a six-month moratorium. The revised ordinance strengthens regulations on setbacks, screening, and bonding requirements. Chairman Jay Paul called it 'a huge step in the right direction.' A Leeward Renewable Energy representative expressed disappointment, warning the company's planned expansion in the county is 'DOA' without variances.

event_title: Georgia Legislators Propose Data Center Moratorium and Restrictions
event_description: Seven bills targeting data centers were introduced in the Georgia legislature, including HB 1012 by Rep. Ruwa Romman (D-Duluth) proposing a statewide moratorium on new data center construction until March 2027. Other bills would eliminate tax breaks or prohibit costs from being passed to residential customers. The bills respond to concerns about energy demand from data centers impacting solar and clean energy development.

event_title: Houston County Solar Farm Features 1000 Sheep in Agrivoltaics Program
event_description: Silicon Ranch's 68 MW Houston Solar Project along I-75 was highlighted for its large-scale agrivoltaics program featuring approximately 1,000 sheep grazing the 705-acre facility. The project, which provides clean energy to Georgia's electric membership cooperatives, demonstrates Silicon Ranch's commitment to regenerative land management. Half of the company's 22 Georgia solar farms are grazed by sheep.

event_title: Grady County Holds Public Hearing on Solar Moratorium Extension
event_description: In a packed meeting that stretched just over an hour, the Grady County Board of Commissioners held a public hearing to consider extending their 30-day moratorium on solar farm permits. Many residents asked for a longer pause before the county moves forward with solar development. Some opposed solar farms citing aesthetics and land use concerns, while others felt solar could bring economic opportunity and tax revenue to the county.

event_title: Grady County Extends Solar Farm Moratorium for Six Months
event_description: The Grady County Board of Commissioners voted to extend the moratorium on solar farm permits for six months, allowing more time for research and to address public concerns. The moratorium is set to expire on August 6, 2026 unless the commission decides to extend it again. This follows a January 23 public hearing where residents expressed divided opinions on solar development.

event_title: SOLARCYCLE Begins Solar Panel Recycling Operations in Cedartown
event_description: SOLARCYCLE announced the start of recycling operations at its 255,000 square foot facility in Cedartown. The facility uses proprietary technology to recover 96% of the value from end-of-life solar panels while achieving 100% landfill diversion. The plant is processing thousands of panels weekly and expects to scale to 1 million panels annually by end of 2026. The adjacent solar glass manufacturing plant is on track to break ground mid-2026.

event_title: Gaskins Solar Farm Operational in Berrien County
event_description: The Gaskins Solar Farm, a 2.2 MW facility developed by Beltline Energy, became operational in Berrien County. The project uses single axis tracking technology and generates approximately 3,920 MWh annually, equivalent to powering about 560 households.

event_title: Irwin County Approves Solar Panel Ordinance Despite Farmer Opposition
event_description: Irwin County approved a solar panel ordinance in January 2024. Local farmers expressed opposition to the measure, with one farmer stating that if commissioners were representing the people, they should have voted against it. The ordinance establishes regulations for solar development in the county.

event_title: Opdenergy Proposes 470 MW Solar Farm Spanning Heard and Coweta Counties
event_description: Opdenergy proposed a 470 MW solar facility spanning approximately 3,000 acres in Heard and Coweta counties near Chattahoochee Bend State Park. The project would generate over $70 million in tax revenue and power approximately 100,000 homes. Construction is planned to begin in 2026 with up to 300 construction jobs at peak.

event_title: Green Power EMC Solar Site Operational in Paulding County
event_description: A Green Power EMC solar site became operational in Paulding County, generating approximately 2,000 MWh of electricity annually. The offset is equivalent to 1,500 metric tons of greenhouse gas emissions and produces enough electricity to serve about 140 EMC households.

event_title: Green Power EMC Solar Site Operational in Barrow County
event_description: A Green Power EMC solar site became operational in Barrow County, generating approximately 4,000 MWh of electricity annually. The offset is equivalent to 2,700 metric tons of greenhouse gas emissions and produces enough electricity to serve about 250 EMC households.

event_title: Solarize Cobb Community Solar Program Launches
event_description: Solarize Cobb, a community-led clean energy group purchasing program, officially launched to make rooftop solar panels more affordable for local residents, businesses and nonprofits. The program was created by a coalition including My Green Earth, Georgia Interfaith Power & Light, Environment Georgia, and Sierra Club Georgia Chapter.

event_title: Cobb EMC Campus Solar and Battery Storage Facility Operational
event_description: Cobb EMC completed installation of approximately 1.85 MW of solar and 1 MW (4 MWh) of battery storage at their campus near Highway 41. The facility provides enough power to supply about 200 homes for a full 12 months and demonstrates the cooperative's commitment to renewable energy.

event_title: Multiple Solar Facilities Operational in Screven County
event_description: Screven County hosts three operational solar facilities: Old Midville Solar (owned by Citizens Enterprises Corporation), Southern Current One LLC, and Haley Solar (owned by Haley Solar LLC). These facilities contribute to renewable energy generation in the region.
project_name: Old Midville Solar; Southern Current One; Haley Solar

event_title: Two Renewvia Energy Solar Farms Operational in Gordon County
event_description: Renewvia Energy, an Atlanta-based company, established two solar energy farms in Gordon County located on Ga. 53 and Ga. 156. The facilities sell power to the Tennessee Valley Authority through North Georgia EMC, which distributes TVA power in the area.

event_title: Hart County Commissioners Discuss Solar Moratorium and Agricultural Land Bill
event_description: The Hart County Board of Commissioners discussed solar development and land use at their March 11, 2025 meeting. Commissioners considered a temporary moratorium on new solar projects until April to allow further analysis of potential impacts. Discussion included state legislation that would allow solar installations on agricultural covenant land without breaching agreements.

event_title: Dade County Approves 90-Day Solar Farm Moratorium
event_description: Dade County approved Resolution R-18-26 imposing a 90-day moratorium on new commercial solar panel facilities in unincorporated areas while the county reviews and drafts new regulations. The measure halts the acceptance and processing of permits for large-scale solar projects intended to sell or distribute power or covering more than 0.5 acres. The moratorium does not apply to rooftop or small-scale systems serving homes or farms.

event_title: Dade County Extends Solar Farm Moratorium for Additional 90 Days
event_description: At the February County Commission work session, Dade County officials voted to extend the county moratorium on solar farms for an additional 90 days. This extension follows the initial Resolution R-18-26 and gives the county more time to develop comprehensive solar regulations.

event_title: EDP Renewables Presents Shy Place Solar Park Proposal to Jasper County
event_description: EDP Renewables personnel attended the Planning and Zoning work session to present plans for the Shy Place Solar Park, a proposed 2,000+ acre solar farm near Rock Eagle Road by the Putnam County line. The economic development director accompanied EDP representatives and is advocating for tax incentives. EDP has advertised plans to begin construction in Jasper County in 2027.

event_title: Jasper County Solar Farm Ordinance Public Hearing Announced
event_description: The Jasper County Planning and Zoning Board announced a public hearing on a proposed solar farm ordinance for February 26, 2026 at 6:00 PM in the Courthouse. The ordinance was proposed by a citizen and developed to establish local regulations fitting Jasper County rather than relying on a generic state-mandated ordinance. More than 50 residents attended an earlier town hall meeting where virtually all comments opposed solar farm development in the county.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves 200 MW Battery Storage Project in Twiggs County
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved construction of a new 200 MW battery energy storage system in Twiggs County southeast of Macon. The BESS is co-located with an existing solar farm and has a projected completion date of 2027. This adds to the growing battery storage capacity being deployed across Georgia.

event_title: Carroll County Approves River Trail Solar Siting Agreement
event_description: Carroll County approved a siting agreement for the River Trail Solar project, a 20 MW utility-scale solar facility. The project is expected to generate $3.9 million in tax revenues for the county over its 35-year lifespan.

event_title: Meriwether Solar Farm Operational in Meriwether County
event_description: The Meriwether Solar Farm, a 3.0 MW facility developed by Beltline Energy using fixed tilt technology, became operational. The facility produces approximately 4,500 MWh per year, enough to power about 643 households. Solar accounts for 100% of electricity generation in the county.

event_title: Stephens County Approves Solar Panel Installation at County Jail
event_description: Stephens County approved installation of a solar panel system adjacent to the county jail. The project is expected to reduce annual electricity costs from $70,000 to under $20,000. The county will receive a 30% federal tax credit rebate. Commissioner Chris Rickman noted the county would be one of the first in the region to implement such a project.

event_title: Spalding County Holds Workshop on Solar District Ordinance
event_description: The Spalding County Board of Commissioners held a workshop on a proposed solar district ordinance to regulate solar generation facilities. The ordinance outlines permissible solar array types in various zoning classifications including integrated systems, rooftop installations, and ground-mounted facilities. Discussion highlighted tensions between landowners wanting to lease land for solar and those preferring traditional farming.

event_title: Georgia Power and Fieldale Farms Break Ground on Baldwin Solar Farm
event_description: Georgia Power and Fieldale Farms Corporation held a groundbreaking ceremony for a new 1.5 MW solar farm in Baldwin on the corner of Duncan Bridge Road and Gainesville Highway. The 6-acre facility will produce approximately 184,000 kWh monthly and offset approximately 1,780,000 pounds of CO2 annually as part of Fieldale's sustainability efforts.

event_title: EDF Renewables Proposes $320M Rock House Solar Farm in McDuffie County
event_description: EDF Renewables North America proposed Rock House Solar, a $320 million, 325 MW solar farm covering nearly 2,900 acres along Randall Hunt Road. The project would generate 250+ construction jobs and up to $850,000 annually in tax revenue for 40 years. Commercial operation was targeted for 2025-2026.

event_title: Columbia Bryson Solar Facility Operational in McDuffie County
event_description: The Columbia Bryson solar facility, owned by Westbound Solar LLC, became operational in McDuffie County, adding to the region's renewable energy capacity.

event_title: Georgia PSC Rejects Reconsideration of December Capacity Expansion
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission voted 3-2 along party lines to reject a petition from environmental groups requesting reconsideration of the December 19, 2025 capacity expansion approval. The petition challenged the PSC decision to certify approximately 9,885 MW of new generation including natural gas plants, battery storage, and solar facilities for Georgia Power. Commissioners Echols, Pridemore, and Robertson voted against reconsideration while Commissioners Blackmon and Heard dissented.

event_title: Bacon County Residents Oppose Silicon Ranch Solar Farm Proposal
event_description: Residents of Bacon County held a community town hall meeting to voice opposition to a proposed Silicon Ranch solar farm. Attendees raised concerns about loss of agricultural land, potential impacts on property values, and the scale of the proposed project in a rural farming community. The meeting drew significant turnout from area landowners and residents who questioned whether utility-scale solar development was appropriate for the county.

event_title: Packed Commissioners Meeting on Silicon Ranch Solar Farm Sparks Backlash
event_description: At a packed Bacon County commissioners meeting, residents demanded answers about how the Silicon Ranch solar project moved forward and whether county leaders were transparent about the process. The project involves nearly 800 acres of land purchased for over $5.1 million, with Silicon Ranch planning to invest more than $300 million in partnership with Green Power EMC. Construction on the first phase is already underway, with panels reportedly being installed approximately 100 feet from some homes. After the meeting, commissioners said they had signed a memorandum of understanding with Silicon Ranch before adopting solar ordinances and formed a volunteer committee to gather information and make recommendations. Residents also raised concerns about a prior Silicon Ranch erosion damage lawsuit in Stewart County.
project_name: Silicon Ranch Bacon County Energy + Agriculture

event_title: Georgia Balcony Solar Bill HB 1304 Sidelined After Utility Opposition
event_description: House Bill 1304, introduced by Rep. Imani Barnes (D-Tucker) with bipartisan support, would have exempted portable plug-in solar devices from interconnection regulations, expanding solar access to renters and those without rooftops. The bill was heard in the Energy, Utilities & Telecommunications Committee but Chairman Don Parsons declined to bring it to a vote. Georgia Power director Wilson Mallard opposed blanket exemptions for small systems, and Georgia EMC cited lineman safety concerns. The bill will not advance this legislative session.
outcome: Bill sidelined; not brought to committee vote

event_title: Jasper County Solar Ordinance Public Hearing Draws Strong Opposition
event_description: The Jasper County Planning and Zoning Board held a public hearing on the proposed solar farm ordinance on February 26. Residents voiced strong opposition, raising concerns about environmental impacts to the Murder Creek ecosystem, potential runoff and pollution from land clearing, and the precedent that large industrial solar farms could set for future data centers and warehouses. No final decision was reached; a follow-up discussion is scheduled for March 12 at 6:00 PM before the Board of Commissioners.

event_title: Qcells Resumes Full Solar Panel Production at Georgia Factories
event_description: Qcells announced its solar panel production is back to normal at its Georgia manufacturing facilities after a temporary pause caused by US Customs and Border Protection detaining shipments of solar cells and polysilicon under UFLPA enforcement. The company had furloughed approximately 1,000 workers across its Dalton and Cartersville plants in late 2025. The Cartersville factory is expected to reach 3.3 GW capacity for ingots, wafers, and cells by end of 2026. Combined with Dalton, the facilities will employ nearly 4,000 workers producing 8.4 GW of solar panels and components annually.

event_title: Data Center Bills Cross Over Georgia Legislature on Crossover Day
event_description: Three significant data center bills survived Crossover Day in the Georgia General Assembly, advancing from one chamber to the other. SB 410 would eliminate existing tax breaks for data centers. HB 559 would shorten the sunset on data center tax breaks from 2031 to 2026. HB 1012 would institute a statewide halt on data center construction, prohibiting local governments from issuing permits, licenses, or certificates for data center construction between July 1, 2026 and March 1, 2027. These bills reflect growing legislative pushback against data center expansion, which has been the primary driver of Georgia Powers massive capacity expansion including solar procurement.
outcome: Bills crossed over; advancing to opposite chambers

event_title: PSC Chairman Shaw Defends Data Center Expansion and Energy Capacity Plan
event_description: Georgia PSC Chairman Jason Shaw published an op-ed in multiple Georgia newspapers defending the December 2025 decision to approve nearly 10,000 MW of new generation capacity for Georgia Power. Shaw revealed that 42% of approved capacity will come from battery storage and solar sources, with 58% from natural gas. He disclosed that the prospective large-load project pipeline, approximately 80% of which are data centers, has grown from 16,000 MW in 2023 to roughly 69,000 MW by December 2025. Shaw acknowledged the core risk: "The biggest fear we have had from day one is what if these loads do not materialize." He also noted that Georgia Power and PSC staff negotiated a customer protection stipulation guaranteeing revenue in 2029-2031 to prevent a projected $20 monthly rate increase from materializing.
outcome: Public defense of capacity expansion plan; customer protections negotiated
source_name: Moultrie Observer; Valdosta Daily Times; Atlanta News First

event_title: Georgia Power Awards Largest Distributed Generation Solar Procurement in History
event_description: Georgia Power announced the completion of its largest distributed generation solar procurement, awarding over 110 MW of new third-party solar generation. The final tranche included 16 new contracts totaling 70 MW approved by the Georgia PSC, building on 12 earlier contracts adding 41 MW. Projects range from 250 kW to 6 MW each under long-term power purchase agreements. Two additional DG RFPs targeting 50 MW each are planned for 2026 and 2027, with projects expected online by 2028.

event_title: Georgia Power Breaks Ground on 260 MW Wadley Battery Storage System
event_description: Georgia Power broke ground on a 260 MW / 1,040 MWh battery energy storage system in Jefferson County near Wadley, adjacent to the existing third-party owned Wadley solar facility and near existing transmission infrastructure. Members of the Jefferson County Board of Commissioners and Wadley City Council joined the ceremony. The project, constructed by Burns & McDonnell, is designed to dispatch stored energy over a four-hour period and is expected to be completed in 2027. This is in addition to four other BESS facilities totaling 765 MW nearing completion across Bibb, Cherokee, Floyd, and Lowndes counties.

event_title: Georgia 2026 Legislative Session Ends With Data Center Bills Stalled
event_description: The Georgia General Assembly concluded its 2026 legislative session on Sine Die, April 2, with key data center energy legislation failing to complete passage. SB 410, which would have repealed data center sales tax exemptions and required data centers to cover infrastructure costs, passed the Senate 32-21 but sat in the House without committee hearings for weeks and appeared dead. HB 1063, which would have codified requirements preventing data center infrastructure costs from being passed to residential ratepayers, passed the House 159-5 but stalled in the Senate. The failure of these bills means the existing framework governing data center energy costs and tax incentives remains unchanged, preserving the status quo that has driven Georgia Powers massive capacity expansion including significant solar procurement.
outcome: Key DC bills failed to pass both chambers; status quo preserved
source_name: WABE; Georgia Watch; Rough Draft Atlanta

event_title: Jasper County P&Z Board Holds Final Discussion on Solar Farm Ordinance
event_description: The Jasper County Planning and Zoning Board held a final discussion of the proposed solar farm ordinance on March 12 at 6:00 PM, following the February 26 public hearing where residents voiced strong opposition. The board reviewed community feedback regarding environmental concerns about the Murder Creek ecosystem and fears that solar farms would set a precedent for data centers and warehouses. The discussion preceded the ordinance moving to the Board of County Commissioners for formal action.
source_name: Jasper County P&Z; Taxpayer's Watchdog Group

event_title: Jasper County Commissioners Add Solar Farms to Not Allowed Uses in Zoning
event_description: The Jasper County Board of County Commissioners considered an ordinance amendment at their April 6 regular meeting that adds "Not Allowed" to the zoning description for Solar Farms, effectively prohibiting large-scale solar development in the county. The action follows months of sustained community opposition including a January town hall, February public hearing, and March P&Z discussion, all of which drew strong resident opposition to the proposed EDP Renewables Shy Place Solar Park and solar development generally.

event_title: Environmental and Faith Groups Sue PSC Over Georgia Power Expansion Approval
event_description: The Southern Environmental Law Center and Sierra Club, representing Georgia Interfaith Power & Light and member churches, filed a 42-page lawsuit in Fulton County Superior Court challenging the Georgia PSC approval of nearly 10 GW of new energy generation for Georgia Power. The groups argue GP never proved all new resources were needed as required by state law, and that overbuilding for data centers that lack signed contracts exposes ratepayers to higher bills. Georgia Power called the suit meritless. The challenge has implications for the renewable energy mix as groups contend more renewables should have been pursued over gas plants.

event_title: Georgia PSC Unanimously Approves Customer Identified Resource Program for Corporate Clean Energy
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission unanimously approved Georgia Power's Customer Identified Resource (CIR) program, also known as "BYONCE" (Bring Your Own Clean Energy). The program allows large commercial and industrial customers, including data center operators, to contract directly with renewable energy developers and connect clean energy projects (solar, battery, wind) to the grid. Companies pay Georgia Power a monthly tariff in exchange for renewable energy credits. The framework allows up to 3 GW of customer-identified resources through 2035, representing the majority of Georgia Power's plan to procure 4 GW of new renewables. The program is expected to open by summer 2026 and could help prevent data center growth from raising bills for other customers.
source_name: Utility Dive; AJC; Canary Media; Grist

event_title: Southern Renewable Energy Association Launches Powering Georgia Initiative
event_description: The Southern Renewable Energy Association officially launched "Powering Georgia," a collaborative statewide initiative to promote affordable clean energy access for all Georgia residents. The initiative brings together stakeholders across the renewable energy sector to advance responsible development of solar energy, wind energy, and transmission solutions in the state.

event_title: Dade County Approves Solar Ordinance Establishing Special Use Permit Framework
event_description: The Dade County Board of Commissioners approved a new ordinance regulating large-scale solar developments following a public hearing and special called meeting. The ordinance establishes a framework requiring a special use permit for solar energy projects, replacing the temporary moratorium (R-18-26) that had been in place since early February 2026. Future proposals will be reviewed by the county special use permit board. Commissioners stated the goal is to protect both landowners and neighboring properties as interest in solar development grows in northwest Georgia.
outcome: Ordinance approved; special use permit required

event_title: New Bethel AME Church Becomes Georgia BRIGHT Solar and Storage Resilience Hub
event_description: New Bethel AME Church in Lithonia installed a 70.11 kW solar system, 41 kWh battery storage, and dual Level II EV chargers through Better Tomorrow Solar, becoming the first commercial pilot participant to pursue battery storage through Georgia BRIGHT and Capital Good Fund. The system covers approximately 80% of the church energy needs and saves over $15,000 per year. Zero up-front cost, funded via Hive Fund, Black Voters Matter, and Georgia BRIGHT. The project is part of the AME Sixth District and Georgia Interfaith Power & Light initiative to install 5 microgrids at Georgia churches by end of 2026, with a long-term goal of equipping 482 churches statewide as community resilience hubs.
project_name: New Bethel AME Church Resilience Hub

event_title: Georgia Power Files for 2,000-6,000 MW All-Source RFP and 385 MW Supplemental CARES Solar
event_description: Georgia Power filed with the PSC to approve final documents for an All-Source Capacity RFP seeking 2,000 to 6,000 MW of new dispatchable capacity resources (thermal, energy storage, battery plus renewables) for 2032-2033 delivery. The filing cites 32 large-load customers driving demand. Separately, GP requested certification of approximately 385 MW of additional supplemental solar under the CARES 2023 program. If approved, the RFP would be issued in Q2 2026 with project selections submitted to PSC in mid-2027. This represents a major expansion of Georgia Power procurement pipeline.

event_title: Kia Georgia and VPS Complete 10 MW Solar Canopy at West Point Auto Plant
event_description: Vehicle Protection Structures (VPS) and Kia Georgia completed a 3.2-million-square-foot solar canopy at Kia West Point auto manufacturing plant, with ribbon cutting on April 24, 2026. The system uses 17,000 bifacial Qcells panels generating 10 MW, enough for approximately 10% of the plant power needs. Built in response to a 2023 hailstorm that damaged over 13,000 vehicles. It is among the largest solar canopy projects of its kind in the Southeast, combining vehicle protection with clean energy generation.
